_comment: SPEC-047 checked-in baseline (AC-24: updated only by an explicit commit, never automatically). Values are medians of 5 runs against scripts/build-spec047-fixture.mjs's fixture, measured in the factory container and padded a little above the observed range so ordinary run-to-run variance doesn't trip AC-23's 15% relative gate on its own. Recalibrated 2026-08-14 (second pass) from the first QUIET factory-container run (SPEC-052#4: firstPage 2184, fullyInteractive 2365, open block 214 — all pre-fix) plus the open-path restructuring that run forced: the container is ~2-3x slower than the dev machine on the open path specifically (vs ~1.2x on the rest of the suite), which the earlier extrapolations under-estimated. The restructuring — unzip loop yields, batched-concurrent media base64, editor-route chunk preloaded from the library view, initial persist deferred to idle, and the first layout deferred out of the mount task via pagination.prime() — cut the local quiet medians from 748/~1000/104 (firstPage/fullyInteractive/openBlock) to 618/758/57, and a 3x-CPU-throttle harness that reproduced the container's pre-fix numbers now measures ~1730 firstPage with no task over ~180. firstPageMs 1800 and fullyInteractiveMs 2300 are those container projections padded; both keep the 2000/8000 absolute ceilings binding (for firstPageMs the absolute is the tighter gate until the next container calibration tightens this row). mainThreadBlockDuringOpenMs stays 130: the post-fix container projection is ~110-135, and 130*1.15=149.5 keeps the relative gate under the 150 absolute so a sub-ceiling regression trips it first. typingLatencyP95Ms 43, mainThreadBlockDuringTypingMs 60, saveMs 1200, scrollFps 45, save/scroll block 90 and heap 30 are unchanged: the quiet container measured 32.1/0/1242/42.8/81/70/26.9 against them, all comfortably inside both gates, and this round's changes do not touch those paths.
_comment_findFirstMatchMs: Not a SPEC-047 budget row: this one belongs to SPEC-017's AC-30 ("searching a 200-page document returns first results within 300 ms"), which lives in e2e/SPEC-017.spec.ts and reads only this key. It shares this file because container calibration belongs in one place; SPEC-047's harness iterates its own BUDGETS table and ignores it. Same two-gate shape as the rows above: the spec's 300ms absolute ceiling, plus this baseline +15%. Added 2026-08-17 as a dev-machine projection, not a container measurement — quiet Mac medians of 5 samples were 29-31ms, the same file run alongside five sibling spec files (753% CPU) measured 42ms, so 30 * 1.24 (container) * 1.4 (in-suite contention) ~= 52ms, padded to 80 to leave room for the host-level contention SPEC-047's header describes. A real regression trips the relative gate at 92ms long before the 300ms ceiling; a first QUIET container run should tighten this row.
